title: Service
description: A service a resident can obtain from government: a birth certificate, a business registration, housing support, a parking permit. The requests profile covers reporting a problem; this covers finding and using a service, which is the most common thing anyone asks a government website. Mirrors Open Referral / HSDS, which remains the source model. This is the fuller definition of schema:GovernmentService; requests/service.schema.json describes the same type at the depth Open311 needs, and a publisher serving both should use this one.

name.description: The service's public name, e.g. 'Apply for a business licence'.

alternateName.description: Other names residents might know this service by.

description.description: A plain-language explanation of the service, shown to residents deciding whether it's the one they need.

url.description: Where more information about this service can be found.

identifier.description: Any scheme-qualified identifiers for this service beyond its `@id`.

serviceCode.description: The publisher's own code. Shared with the requests profile.

keywords.description: Search terms residents might use to find this service.

areaServed.description: The `Jurisdiction` this service is available in.

serviceStatus.description: Whether the service is currently available. HSDS distinguishes defunct from temporarily closed because a resident needs to know whether to come back. Optional at Core conformance, because Open311 service catalogues carry no status field and requiring it would make them unrepresentable. Required at Standard: a service listing that cannot say whether the service still exists is of limited use.

lifeEvent.description: The life events this service relates to. People look for services by circumstance - having a baby, losing a job, moving home - not by the department that happens to run them, which is why the EU Single Digital Gateway organises services this way.

eligibility.description: Who may use the service. schema:PeopleAudience already carries age and geography; the free-text criterion carries what a structured audience cannot express.

eligibilityCriteria.description: Conditions no structured field captures - residency, income, tenure, immigration status.

applicationProcess.description: How to apply, in plain language. HSDS treats this as central and it is what residents actually need; a service described without it is a listing rather than a route to anything.

requiredDocument.description: What an applicant must bring or supply. The single most common reason an application fails at the counter.

optional.description: True where an alternative is accepted.

cost.description: What it costs. A free service must say so explicitly rather than omitting the field, because absence reads as unknown.

waiverAvailable.description: Whether a fee waiver or reduction exists. Publishing the fee without the waiver deters exactly the people the waiver is for.

processingTime.description: Expected time to completion, as an ISO 8601 duration.

availableChannel.description: schema:ServiceChannel - online, phone, in person, post.

availableAtLocation.description: Where the service is delivered in person, and when. HSDS keeps this as a separate join because a service and a location are independent things with a many-to-many relationship.

interpretationAvailable.description: Whether interpretation is offered for languages not listed.

accessibilityNote.description: Accommodations available for residents with disabilities.

relatedLegislation.description: The provision the service is delivered under.

dateModified.description: When this record was last updated.

sourceDataset.description: The `Dataset` this record was published as part of.
